decisive_items: Round and smooth surface mass arising from the isthmus of the right tube
Fleshy mass bulging from the right cornual area
Positive for vimentin, desmin, smooth muscle actin, and estrogen and progesterone receptors
response.rationale: Laparoscopic findings localize the mass to the fallopian tube, and the IHC profile (desmin, SMA, ER/PR positive; CD34 and pan-cytokeratin negative) is characteristic of a smooth muscle tumor. The benign features (well-demarcated, no mitotic atypia) and tubal origin distinguish it from uterine leiomyoma and malignancy.

rejected.why: STUMP is a uterine diagnosis, but the mass is tubal; also benign features and well-demarcated border argue against uncertain malignant potential.
Uterine leiomyoma is contradicted by the tubal origin on laparoscopy; the mass is adnexal, not uterine.
Leiomyosarcoma is excluded by benign frozen section, lack of mitotic atypia, and well-demarcated border.
Adenomyosis is a uterine wall condition; pathology shows spindle/epithelioid cells and IHC smooth muscle markers, not endometrial glands/stroma.
